key_insight: The paper aims to make visual-reasoning feedback more trustworthy by distinguishing corrections grounded in visual evidence from changes driven by language priors or response style.
problem_solved: Verifiable rewards indicate whether an answer is correct but provide limited help locating visual-reasoning errors. Teacher-generated token-level corrections offer finer guidance, yet may mix genuine visual improvements with unrelated changes.
method: Use multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for task-level supervision.
Complement rewards with on-policy self-distillation: a privileged teacher receives an evidence-centered visual view and supplies dense token-level corrections.
Target visual attribution of those corrections; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify the attribution mechanism.
impact: This direction could help practitioners train models that learn from visual evidence rather than incidental teacher behavior. The supplied excerpt does not report experiments or measured gains.

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
